a1-n-dame: At a fancy restaurant the waiter says: 'Good evening, ladies and gentlemen.' He speaks to an elegant, polite woman in a long dress. How do you call such a woman?
A sign on the door of a washroom shows a woman in a dress. A friend says it is for the female guests, in a formal style.
In a board game you move round pieces diagonally on a black and white board, and one piece is called 'queen' in chess. Which noun can mean 'lady' or 'queen' (in cards or chess)?
a1-n-kindergarten: Your three-year-old son goes to a place every morning where children play, sing and paint before school age.
A mother drops her daughter at a building with a playground and a teacher, and goes to work. The child is too young for school.
A parent asks the neighbour where the children play together and learn before their first school year. Which noun means 'nursery school'?
a1-v-sitzen: You are on the bus and all the chairs are taken, but you have found a place and rest your legs.
A bird lands on the branch of a tree and stays on it without moving.
You work at a desk all day. Your back hurts because you rest on a chair for eight hours. Which verb means 'to sit'?
a1-n-sonne: In summer the sky is blue and a big yellow ball gives you light and heat. You put on sun cream.
You close the curtains because the bright star in the sky shines straight into your face.
The earth goes round it once a year. Which noun means 'sun'?
a1-n-restaurant: On Saturday evening you and your partner go to a place where waiters bring food to your table and you pay at the end.
You do not feel like cooking tonight, so you phone to reserve a table for four at 8 p.m.
Your friend says: 'Let's eat out. There is a nice Italian place near the station.' Which noun means 'restaurant'?
a1-adj-hell: You draw the curtains in the morning and the room is full of sunshine, not dark at all.
A shop sells paint in colours such as dark blue and pale blue. You choose the colour with more white in it.
A lamp shines so strongly that your eyes hurt. Which adjective means 'light' or 'bright'?
a1-n-oma: On Sundays you visit a kind old woman who bakes apple cake. She is the mother of your mum.
A little girl runs to the door and shouts that her dad's mother has arrived with a bag of presents. What does she call her in a warm, short way?
At the family party the youngest child sits on the lap of the white-haired woman and calls her by a loving name. Which noun means 'grandma'?
a1-v-anmachen: It is dark in the living room. You press the switch and make the lamp work.
Your friend wants to watch the news, so he presses the button on the remote and the screen starts up.
In winter you put a match to the wood so that the fireplace starts burning. Which verb means 'to turn on' or 'to light'?
a1-n-chef: At work you have a problem. You knock on the door of the person who is in charge of the whole department.
A waiter says: 'I must ask the person who runs this restaurant if we can give you a discount.'
You tell your friend that you got a raise, because the person who leads your team is happy with your work. Which noun means 'boss' (male)?
a1-adv-draussen: It is a sunny day. The children are not in the house, but are playing in the garden.
The restaurant has tables inside and some on the pavement. You prefer to sit in the fresh air.
Your friend asks: 'Where are the kids?' You point through the window: 'They are not in the room, they are ...' Which adverb means 'outside'?
a1-n-wiedersehen: After ten years you meet your old school friends again, and you hug each other in tears of joy.
At the end of a phone call you say a polite word that means you hope to meet or talk again.
The sign on the shop door says: 'Thank you for your visit, goodbye.' Which noun is used in the phrase for 'goodbye'? It also means 'reunion'.
a1-pr-mich: You look in the mirror and point at yourself: 'It is a photo of ...' Which word means 'me' as an object?
Your friend calls your name. You say: 'You can phone ... tomorrow.' Which pronoun means 'me' after a verb?
A child hurts herself and says: 'I washed ...' meaning that she washed herself. Which word means 'me, myself'?
a1-n-mund: The dentist says: 'Please open wide.' She looks inside the part of your face with your teeth and tongue.
You eat an apple. What part of your face do you use to bite and chew?
A baby is hungry and cries. The mother puts the spoon to its lips. Which noun means 'mouth'?
a1-v-anziehen: It is cold outside. Before you leave the house you take a coat from the hook and put your arms in the sleeves.
In the morning you help your small daughter to put her shirt and trousers on.
A magnet pulls small nails towards it, and a good film pulls viewers. Which verb can mean 'to dress', 'to put on' or 'to attract'?
a1-adj-laut: Your neighbours play music so strongly that you cannot sleep. How would you describe the music?
A child screams in the playground and everyone covers their ears.
The opposite of quiet: the traffic on the main road is full of noise. Which adjective means 'loud'?
a1-n-februar: The shortest month of the year comes after January and before March. Sometimes it has 29 days.
Carnival and Valentine's Day take place in this winter month.
On a calendar the second page shows this month. Which noun means 'February'?
a1-n-anruf: Your phone rings at 8 p.m. It is your mother and she wants to talk.
The secretary says to the boss: 'There was someone on the line for you while you were in the meeting.'
You missed a notice on your screen showing that someone tried to reach you. Which noun means 'phone call'?
a1-v-kaufen: In the supermarket you put milk, bread and cheese on the belt and give the cashier money.
You see a nice jacket in a shop window. You go in, try it on and take it home after you hand over your card.
Your friend says: 'I want to get a new phone because mine is broken.' Which verb means 'to buy'?
a1-n-wetter: You look out of the window and see clouds and rain. Then you check the forecast on your phone.
The newsreader says: 'Tomorrow it will be sunny with 25 degrees in the south.'
Your friend asks if you want to go on a picnic. You say it depends on whether it rains or the sun shines. Which noun means 'weather'?
a1-n-hotel: You travel to Berlin for three days. You book a place where you sleep in a room and have breakfast, and pay for each night.
A tourist asks the taxi driver to take him to the building with a lobby and a front desk where his room is booked.
For your holiday you choose between a flat and a building with many rooms and staff. Which noun means 'hotel'?
a1-n-tomate: You slice a round red vegetable for your salad. It has many small seeds inside.
Your mother makes a sauce for the pasta with red fruits from the garden and some basil.
On a pizza there is cheese and a sauce made from a red fruit. Which noun means 'tomato'?
a1-adv-wo: You cannot find your keys and ask your wife about the place where they are.
You are in a new city and need a pharmacy. You ask a passer-by about its position.
Your friend says he has moved. You ask about the place he lives in now. Which word means 'where'?
a1-v-mitbringen: You are invited to a dinner and your host asks you to carry a bottle of wine and a dessert with you.
Your sister is coming back from Italy and says she will have a gift for you in her suitcase.
The teacher says: 'Tomorrow, please come with your dictionary.' Which verb means 'to bring along'?
a1-adj-schwarz: You wear a suit to a funeral. It is the colour of coal and the night sky.
A cat sits in the dark and you can barely see it, because it is the opposite colour of white.
At the cafe you order a drink with no milk, the colour of ink. Which adjective means 'black'?
a1-n-hobby: On a form it asks what you do for fun in your free time. You write: painting and playing guitar.
A new colleague asks you what you like to do after work. You say that you love collecting stamps.
Which noun, borrowed from English, means 'hobby'?
a1-n-anzeige: You look in the newspaper and find a small text with a picture that offers a flat for rent.
On the website there is a banner that tries to sell you shoes while you read the news.
A screen at the station shows when the next train comes. Which noun can mean 'advertisement' or 'display'?
a1-n-liter: At the petrol station you put fifty of these into your car. Fuel is sold by this measure of volume.
A bottle of water at the supermarket contains 1,000 millilitres. Which unit is that?
A recipe asks for half a unit of milk, that is 500 ml. Which noun means 'litre'?
a1-v-druecken: The door does not open when you pull it. You put your hand flat against it and push.
You put your finger on the doorbell button until it rings.
At the airport you meet your old friend and take her in your arms tightly. Which verb means 'to press, push' or 'to hug'?
a1-n-kuchen: For a birthday party your aunt bakes something sweet in the oven with flour, eggs and sugar, and cuts it into pieces.
In the cafe you order a piece of something sweet with fruit and cream to eat with your tea.
On Sunday afternoon the family sits together with coffee and a sweet baked dish. Which noun means 'cake'?
a1-n-abend: The sun goes down, you finish work and come home to have dinner. What part of the day is it?
A friend says: 'Let's meet after dinner, around eight o'clock.' Which noun refers to this time of day?
When you leave the office, it is neither morning nor afternoon, and it is getting dark. Which noun means 'evening'?
a1-pr-man: A sign in the museum says that visitors must not take photos. You want to explain a general rule that applies to people in general. Which small word means 'one' or 'you' in general?
A friend asks how to get a visa. You say: 'First you fill in a form, then you wait.' You speak about people in general, not about a particular person.
A teacher explains: 'Everybody writes it this way.' Which indefinite pronoun means 'one, you, they'?
a1-adj-weiblich: On a form there are two boxes for sex: male and the other one. A woman ticks it.
In class the teacher explains the nouns: some are masculine, some neuter, and some are of the gender that goes with women.
A zoo sign tells you that the animal in the cage is a lioness, not a lion. Which adjective means 'female'?
a1-v-ankommen: Your train from Munich gets to the station in Berlin at 10 a.m. You step out onto the platform.
After a long drive you phone your mother and say: 'We have got to the hotel safely.'
The flight is delayed. The airport screen shows that the plane has not yet landed. Which verb means 'to arrive'?
a1-n-lieblings: A friend asks you about your best-liked song. You say: 'This is my ... song.' Which word, joined to other words, means 'favourite'?
A child shows you the toy he loves most and calls it his ... toy.
At the restaurant the waiter asks about your most-loved dish. Which word placed before a noun means 'favourite'?
a1-adv-nicht: The waiter offers you more soup, but you have had enough. You say: 'No, thank you, I do ... want any.'
Your friend asks if you like fish. You make a face and shake your head: 'I do ... like it.'
You say the door is open, but the opposite is true. You make a sentence negative. Which adverb means 'not'?
a1-n-koffer: You go on a long trip and pack your clothes and shoes into a big box with wheels and a handle.
At the airport you wait at the belt for your luggage to come out.
The taxi driver puts your big, heavy luggage in the boot. Which noun means 'suitcase'?
a1-n-apfel: You take a round red or green fruit from the bowl and bite into it. It keeps the doctor away, as they say.
For a snack your mother cuts a crunchy fruit into slices and gives them to you.
At the market you buy a kilo of round fruits that grow on trees, are red or green and make juice. Which noun means 'apple'?
a1-v-schlafen: It is midnight. You turn off the light, close your eyes and rest in your bed until morning.
The baby is quiet in the cradle and does not move. Everyone speaks softly.
A friend yawns and says: 'I have not rested enough for three days.' Which verb means 'to sleep'?
a1-n-fieber: You feel hot and cold at the same time. The thermometer shows 39 degrees and the doctor says that your body temperature is too high.
Your child is sick and her forehead is very warm. The nurse measures it with a thermometer.
The doctor says: 'You must stay in bed. Your temperature is high.' Which noun means 'fever'?
a1-n-baum: In the park a tall plant with a thick trunk, branches and green leaves gives shade.
In autumn the leaves of the big plants fall to the ground and children rake them.
A squirrel climbs up a trunk with branches and leaves. Which noun means 'tree'?
a1-adj-billig: In the market you find a shirt for only 5 euros. It does not cost much.
You compare two phones: one costs 800 euros and the other only 100. The second one does not cost a lot.
The opposite of expensive: a friend says: 'I found a hotel that doesn't cost much.' Which adjective means 'cheap'?
a1-n-oktober: The leaves turn red and yellow, and the tenth month begins after September.
The big beer festival in Munich ends in the first days of this month.
On a calendar the tenth page shows this month. Which noun means 'October'?
a1-v-mitkommen: Your friends are going to the cinema. They say: 'Do you want to join us?' You say yes.
You go for a walk fast and your friend cannot go as quickly, so you wait. She asks you to slow down so she can follow your pace.
A colleague asks: 'Are you going to the party tonight?' You say: 'I will go with you.' Which verb means 'to come along'?
a1-n-film: On Friday you go to the cinema with your friends and watch a story on a big screen.
Your favourite actor stars in a new picture. You buy popcorn and sit in the dark room.
At home you choose something to watch on a streaming service with a story and actors. Which noun means 'film, movie'?
a1-n-see: On a hot summer day you go swimming in a big body of fresh water surrounded by land.
In the mountains there is a big clear body of water in a valley, with boats and a beach.
Your family has a picnic at the water's edge and the children jump in. It is not a river or the sea. Which noun means 'lake'?
a1-adv-lieber: Your friend asks: 'Tea or coffee?' You answer that you would prefer tea. Which adverb shows what you prefer?
The waiter asks: 'Fish or meat?' You say you like fish more. Which word means 'rather'?
You say: 'I would prefer to stay at home tonight than go out.' Which adverb means 'rather'?
a1-n-nummer: You tell the receptionist the digits on your room key: 305. What are these digits together?
Somebody asks you to write down your phone digits on a piece of paper.
A runner wears a sign with 42 on her shirt for the race. Which noun means 'number'?
a1-v-einkaufen: On Saturday you take a bag and go to the supermarket to get food for the week.
Your mother writes a list with milk, bread and eggs, and sends you to the shops.
Before Christmas the town centre is full of people who are buying presents. Which verb means 'to shop'?
a1-n-august: It is the hottest month. School is out and many people go on holiday. It comes after July.
The eighth month of the year has 31 days and is often sunny.
On a calendar the eighth page shows this month. Which noun means 'August'?
a1-adj-ruhig: The library is silent and you can concentrate. How would you describe it?
The baby is not crying, and everyone is relaxed. The street where you live has hardly any traffic and no noise.
Your friend is not nervous before the exam and sits there with a smile. Which adjective means 'calm, quiet'?
a1-n-ansage: On the train a voice says: 'The next stop is Cologne.' What is it called?
At the airport a loudspeaker says that the flight to Rome is delayed.
At the supermarket the loudspeaker says: 'Attention please, the shop closes in ten minutes.' Which noun means 'announcement'?
a1-pr-ich: You talk about yourself and point at your chest. Which word do you use for 'I'?
The teacher asks: 'Who has done the homework?' You raise your hand and say: '... have!' Which pronoun means 'I'?
A friend asks who wants some cake. You say you do. Which word means 'I'?
a1-v-essen: At lunchtime you sit down with a plate of rice and chicken and use your fork.
The whole family sits around the table and takes the food in their mouths with spoons.
A friend says: 'I am hungry. Let's put something in our stomachs.' Which verb means 'to eat'?
a1-n-dezember: It is cold, there is snow in many places, and the year ends. Christmas comes in this month.
It is the twelfth and last month of the year. People get ready for New Year's Eve.
On a calendar the last page shows this month. Which noun means 'December'?
a1-n-appetit: Before you start eating, the waiter says: 'Enjoy your meal.' You feel the wish to eat and your stomach rumbles.
You are sick and don't want to eat anything. The doctor asks if you have a desire for food.
Your mother cooks soup and says: 'I hope you are hungry!' Which noun means 'appetite'?
a1-n-anschluss: Your train is late, so you miss the second train that you wanted to take to the next city.
You plug a cable into the little hole on the back of the computer to connect the printer.
At the airport the sign says: 'Flight changes: your onward flight leaves from gate B.' Which noun means 'connection'?
a1-v-kennen: You meet a man at a party and your friend says: 'Oh, I have met him before.' What does your friend do?
A tourist asks you about a restaurant. You say: 'Yes, I have been there many times, I am familiar with it.'
A teacher asks if you have heard of the writer Goethe. You say you are acquainted with his work. Which verb means 'to know' (a person or a place)?
a1-adv-gerade: The phone rings while you are cooking. You say: 'Sorry, I am busy at this very moment.'
A friend asks: 'Where is Anna?' You answer: 'She left a minute ago.' Which adverb means 'just now'?
You look up from the book and say that you are reading at this very second. Which adverb means 'right now'?
a1-adj-einfach: The teacher gives an exercise that every student can solve in one minute. It is not hard.
A recipe has only three steps and few ingredients. How would you describe it?
The instructions for the new phone are clear and easy to follow. Which adjective means 'simple, easy'?
a1-n-miete: At the beginning of every month you transfer money to the owner of your flat.
Your landlord says that from next year the sum you pay each month for the flat will go up.
A friend says: 'My flat is nice but the monthly cost for living there is too high.' Which noun means 'rent'?
a1-n-viertelstunde: The bus comes every fifteen minutes. How long do you wait at most?
You say to your friend: 'Wait for me, I will be ready in 15 minutes.'
The doctor says: 'You must wait for the result.' It takes 15 minutes. Which noun means 'quarter of an hour'?
a1-n-salz: The soup is boring and has no taste. You take a white powder from a small shaker and put some on.
You cook pasta and the recipe says to put a spoonful of the white crystals in the water.
At the table you ask your neighbour to pass the shaker next to the pepper. Which noun means 'salt'?
a1-v-heiraten: Your cousin and his girlfriend are going to the registry office next month and will become husband and wife.
A friend shows you her ring and says: 'We have decided that we will be husband and wife in June.'
A man asks his girlfriend to be his wife for life. Which verb means 'to get married'?
a1-n-sprache: You learn German at an evening school. It is a means of speaking and writing which people of one country use.
In Switzerland people speak German, French and Italian. What are these three?
A friend says: 'I speak three of them: Bengali, English and a little German.' Which noun means 'language'?
a1-n-schild: At the side of the road there is a board with a red circle and a number: 30. You must drive slowly.
On the door of the office a plate says the name of the doctor.
A board in the park shows a picture of a dog with a red line through it. Which noun means 'sign'?
a1-adj-gruen: In spring the grass and the leaves on the trees have this colour.
At the traffic light you can go when the light shows this colour.
You mix blue and yellow and get a new colour, like a frog. Which adjective means 'green'?
a1-v-lesen: In the evening you sit on the sofa and look at the pages of a novel and follow the words with your eyes.
At the breakfast table your father looks at the newspaper and takes in the news.
The teacher says: 'Please say the text aloud from the book.' Which verb means 'to read'?
a1-n-vorsicht: The floor is wet and a yellow sign warns people not to slip. The sign says to be careful.
The mother tells the child at the road: 'Be careful, there are cars!' Which noun is the warning?
At work, a box says: 'Handle with care. Glass.' Which noun means 'caution'?
a1-adv-meist: You have breakfast at 7 a.m. nearly every day, but on Sundays you sleep late. What is your usual habit?
A friend asks if you take the bus. You say: 'In most cases, yes, apart from when it rains and I take a taxi.'
A colleague says: 'On most days, I work from home.' Which adverb means 'mostly'?
a1-n-praktikum: A student works for three months in a company to learn what the job is like, but is not paid much.
Before you finish your studies, the university requires that you gain some experience at a firm.
A young person says: 'Next summer I will do a short period of work to learn the job in a hospital.' Which noun means 'internship'?
a1-pr-dein: You see your friend's umbrella and ask: 'Is this ... umbrella?' Which word means 'your' (informal)?
You talk to your brother: 'Where is ... phone?' Which possessive means 'your' for a friend or family?
You tell a classmate: 'I like ... idea.' Which informal word means 'your'?
a1-n-wochenende: On Friday evening you finish work, and you have two days without school or the office: Saturday and Sunday.
You ask your friend: 'What are you doing on Saturday and Sunday?'
The shops are closed on Sundays, so you do your shopping before the days off begin. Which noun means 'weekend'?
a1-v-klicken: You move the mouse to the button on the screen and press it with your finger to open the page.
The teacher says: 'Go to the website and then use the left mouse button on the link.'
On the webshop you choose the shoes and then press the 'buy' button with your mouse. Which verb means 'to click'?
a1-n-pruefung: Tomorrow you must sit at a desk for two hours and answer questions to get your certificate. You are nervous.
A mechanic looks at your car to see if it is safe to drive, and it passes.
At the end of the course you write a big test with a grade. Which noun means 'exam'?
a1-n-schuh: You go for a walk in the rain, but you forgot to put on the things that protect your feet. They are wet.
In a shop you try on a leather item for your foot, size 42, and walk around.
At the door of the flat, people take off the things on their feet and leave them on a rack. Which noun means 'shoe'?
a1-adj-wunderbar: You have a holiday at the beach, the sun is shining and the food is delicious. You tell your friend that it is fantastic.
Your friend plays the violin and everyone in the room is amazed at how beautiful the music is.
A colleague asks: 'How was the concert?' You say it was extremely good, better than great. Which adjective means 'wonderful'?
a1-n-geschenk: For your friend's birthday you buy a book and wrap it in colourful paper with a bow.
At Christmas there are many wrapped boxes under the tree for everyone in the family.
You are invited to a party. You bring a small gift for the host. Which noun means 'gift, present'?
a1-v-wohnen: You rent a flat on the third floor of a building in Berlin and sleep there every night. Where do you stay?
A friend asks: 'Do you have your own place, or do you stay with your parents?'
A new colleague asks you in which city you have your home. Which verb means 'to live' (in a place)?
a1-n-prospekt: At the travel agency you take a colourful folded paper with pictures and prices of hotels in Spain.
A shop puts printed pages in your mailbox with this week's special offers.
At the tourist office you pick up a small printed booklet with information about the town. Which noun means 'brochure, leaflet'?
a1-n-zug: At the station you wait on the platform for a long vehicle on rails that takes you from Hamburg to Munich.
The conductor checks your ticket in the long line of carriages that moves on tracks.
Instead of flying you decide to travel by a vehicle that runs on rails and stops at many stations. Which noun means 'train'?
a1-adv-vielleicht: Your friend asks: 'Will you come to the party?' You are not sure, there is a chance, but you have not decided.
A colleague asks if it will rain tomorrow. You say that it is possible, but you do not know for certain.
You are not certain about your answer and say: 'It is possible.' Which adverb means 'maybe'?
a1-v-liegen: You are tired and rest flat on the sofa with your legs stretched out.
A book is on the table. It is not standing, it is flat on the surface.
A tourist asks you: 'Where is Hamburg?' You say it is in the north of the country. Which verb means 'to lie' or 'to be situated'?
a1-n-abfahrt: At the station a sign shows that the train to Cologne leaves at 10:15. What does the board show?
You are late and run to the bus. The driver closes the doors and the bus is already moving away.
The timetable has two columns: arrival and the time when the vehicle goes. Which noun means 'departure'?
a1-n-bahnsteig: You wait for the train at the station on a raised area beside the tracks, at number 4.
The announcement says: 'The train to Munich arrives at number 7.' Where do you stand?
A woman asks you: 'Where do I wait for my train?' You point to the long strip of ground beside the rails. Which noun means 'platform' (at a station)?
a1-adj-krank: You have a cold, a fever and a cough, so you stay in bed and do not go to work.
Your child cannot go to school today because she does not feel well and has a high temperature.
The opposite of healthy: your colleague is not at the office. Which adjective means 'sick, ill'?
a1-n-einzelzimmer: You travel alone on business and book a room in a hotel for one person with one bed.
At the reception the clerk asks: 'For how many persons?' You say: 'Only for me.' What kind of room do you want?
A couple needs a double room, but you are travelling alone. Which noun means 'single room'?
a1-v-helfen: Your neighbour carries heavy boxes up the stairs. You take one end and give a hand.
A child cannot tie his shoes. His mother ties them for him so that he can walk.
A tourist is lost. You show him the way. Which verb means 'to help'?
a1-n-maschine: In the laundry room you put your clothes into a big device with a round door that washes them.
At the factory a large device with moving parts makes thousands of bottles every day.
The coffee device in the office is broken. Which noun means 'machine'?
a1-n-plan: You open a drawing of the city on your phone to find the way to the museum.
Before your holiday you write a list of what you will do each day, so that everything is organised.
At the train station there is a timetable with all the trains. Which noun can mean 'plan', 'map' or 'schedule'?
a1-pr-welcher: In a shop you hold two jackets and ask your friend to choose: 'The red or the blue? ... one do you like?' Which word means 'which'?
A waiter holds two cakes and asks you to pick one. You ask him about the options. Which question word means 'which'?
You point at three bags on a shelf and ask the seller about the one you should buy. Which word means 'which'?
a1-n-rechnung: At the end of the dinner the waiter brings a paper with the total amount you must pay.
At the end of the month the electricity company sends you a letter with the amount you owe for the power.
A teacher writes: 3 + 4 = 7 and says the working out is correct. Which noun can mean 'bill' or 'calculation'?
a1-v-spielen: The children run in the garden and play with a ball and toys.
At the weekend you and your friends take out the guitar and make music.
In the evening the family sits around the table with cards and has fun. Which verb means 'to play'?
a1-adj-selbstaendig: A woman has no boss and runs her own small shop. She works for herself.
A teenager moves out of the house and washes, cooks and pays for everything without his parents' help.
On a form for your job there is a box if you work for yourself or for a company. Which adjective means 'independent'?
a1-adv-mehr: At the table you say: 'Could I have a larger amount of rice, please?' Which word means 'more'?
You have two euros, but you need five. You say: 'I need a greater amount of money.'
The teacher says: 'You have to practise a greater amount if you want to improve.' Which adverb means 'more'?
a1-n-grad: The thermometer shows 25, which is warm. What is the unit for temperature?
The weather forecast says: 'Tomorrow it will be minus two.' Which unit does the forecaster use?
A teacher draws a circle on the board and says it has 360 of them. Which noun means 'degree'?
a1-n-satz: The teacher writes on the board: 'I go to school.' It starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.
A student writes an essay and uses many short groups of words with a verb and a subject.
Your homework asks you to make a complete line with the new word. Which noun means 'sentence'?
a1-v-nehmen: The waiter asks what you would like. You say: 'I will choose the soup.'
You reach out and pick up a piece of cake from the plate.
A friend asks: 'How will you get to the airport?' You say you will use the bus. Which verb means 'to take'?
a1-n-auto: You do not take the bus to work, but drive on four wheels with your own engine and steering wheel.
At the petrol station you fill up your vehicle and then clean the windows.
Your father buys a new vehicle for the family. It is blue and has five doors. Which noun means 'car'?
a1-n-kueche: In your flat the room with a cooker, a fridge and a sink is where you prepare your meals.
A restaurant is famous for its Italian style of cooking. Which noun means this way of cooking?
Your mother is cooking in the room next to the living room. Which noun means 'kitchen'?
a1-n-verkaeufer: In the shoe shop a man in a uniform asks if you need help and brings you a pair in your size.
At the market a man stands behind a table full of fruit and shouts the prices.
